item.title: From Iran to Uganda, internet shutdowns batter economies
item.description: The economic toll of digital blackouts hit US$20 billion last year. Citizens are adapting with new tech to skirt government controls.

item.title: Declared a terrorist for bringing renewable power to Philippine communities
item.description: Accusing activists of having links to terrorism has led to non-profit funds being frozen and local climate projects being delayed or scrapped.

item.title: Indonesia scraps permits of firms blamed for worsening Sumatra floods, landslides
item.description: Indonesia has revoked the permits of 28 companies after a post–Cyclone Senyar audit found environmental violations that authorities say worsened deadly floods and landslides in Sumatra in late 2025, which killed about 1,200 people.

item.title: Climate action can unlock Southeast Asia’s future competitiveness
item.description: A deeper transition is a downpayment on the region’s future competitiveness in an increasingly climate-sensitive world.

item.title: Is it time to ‘save the whales’ all over again?
item.description: Forty years after the end of commercial hunting, whales face an increasing threat from global shipping.

item.title: Birth of biggest ever trade bloc troubles environmental experts
item.description: After 25 years, the EU and Mercosur have finalised a trade deal that some experts say could increase emissions and undermine green policies.

item.title: Analysis: EVs just outsold petrol cars in EU for first time ever
item.description: Sales of electric vehicles (EVs) overtook standard petrol cars in the EU for the first time in December 2025, according to new figures released by industry group the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA).

item.title: Explainer: Why gas plays a minimal role in China’s climate strategy
item.description: Ten years ago, switching from burning coal to gas was a key element of China’s policy to reduce severe air pollution.

item.title: What one year of Trump’s climate censorship reveals
item.description: Here's what groups tracking and preserving climate data have found – and what could be next.

item.title: China enters race to host High Seas Treaty HQ
item.description: Considered a “significant escalation” in its global governance aims, China is up against Chile and Belgium to host the treaty’s secretariat.
